You are implementing requirements in the Apache ECharts repository at /workspace.
The source state is ECharts v5.5.0 (TypeScript, sources under src/). Each requirement corresponds to a REAL upstream
apache/echarts pull request whose number is given below. Implement the change the way upstream did wherever you can
recall it, and ALWAYS use exactly the public option/field names quoted in the requirement text.

WORKFLOW RULES
- First read your requirement file: /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml (full acceptance criteria).
- Explore the real code with Grep/Read before editing. Make surgical edits with the Edit tool; never rewrite whole files.
- Keep TypeScript compiling. When you add a public option you MUST also extend its option interface
  (e.g. src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts, src/util/types.ts, or the relevant series/component *Model.ts option interface),
  otherwise `npx tsc --noEmit` will fail. Also remember that many option types are consumed by test/ut and by
  the dts build.
- Verify with: cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false <testPathPattern>
  The whole suite runs in ~15s: `npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`.
  You may run `cd /workspace && npx tsc --noEmit` at the END of your cluster (it takes ~60s) to confirm types.
- ADD A FOCUSED UNIT TEST whenever the behaviour is headlessly testable. Put it under test/ut/spec/... following the
  existing layout (look at neighbours for the mandatory Apache license header at the top of every new .ts file, and
  for the `createChart` helper in test/ut/core/utHelper.ts). Any test you add MUST pass before you commit.
- NEVER run: npm install, npm run build, git add, git commit, git checkout, git reset, git stash, git clean.
  Other agents are concurrently editing OTHER files in this same working tree. Do not touch files outside your
  cluster scope; if you think you must, note it in your report instead of doing it.
- If a file you need was already changed by another cluster, just work with its current content.

COMMIT PROTOCOL (mandatory, one commit per requirement)
After you finish and verify EACH requirement, run:
    /tmp/commit_req.sh <slug> <path1> <path2> ...
listing every file you created/changed for THAT requirement only, as paths relative to /workspace.
The script serializes via flock, stages only those paths, writes requirement_patches/<slug>.diff and commits.
It prints "COMMITTED <slug> (<sha>)" on success. On error it explains why - fix the cause and rerun it.
Work strictly one requirement at a time: implement -> verify -> commit -> next requirement.
Never batch two requirements into one commit. Never leave a requirement uncommitted.

Finally return the JSON report described by your output schema.

## YOUR CLUSTER: "visualmap"
Your file scope (do not edit outside it): src/component/visualMap/**, test/ut/spec/component/visualMap/**

Implement the following 2 requirement(s) IN THIS ORDER, committing each one separately with
/tmp/commit_req.sh before starting the next:

### 1. slug: visualmap-disabled-pointer-cursor  (upstream apache/echarts PR #20551)
With piecewise visualMap `selectedMode: false` the pieces still show a pointer cursor and look clickable. In src/component/visualMap/PiecewiseView.ts (_renderItems / the itemGroup creation with `cursor: 'pointer'` and the onclick binding) make the rendered pieces AND their labels non-interactive when selectedMode is false: no pointer cursor, silent display content, no click handler. Selectable modes ('single'/'multiple'/true) must behave exactly as today. Add a unit test asserting the cursor/silent difference.

### 2. slug: visualmap-handle-label-collision  (upstream apache/echarts PR #20249)
In a horizontal continuous visualMap using `itemWidth/itemHeight` sizing, the drag handle's label collides with neighbouring UI (the end text / the bar). In src/component/visualMap/ContinuousView.ts look at _updateHandle / the handle label positioning (`handleLabels`, `_orient === 'horizontal'`, textAlign/textVerticalAlign and the offset applied) and place the label so it no longer overlaps in the horizontal layout while vertical layouts stay unchanged.

Remember: read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml for each one - the yaml "Acceptance signals" section is the
contract you are graded on. Prefer the smallest faithful change that satisfies it. At the very end of the cluster,
run the full unit suite (`cd /workspace && npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false`) and
`cd /workspace && npx tsc --noEmit`, then run `cd /workspace && git status --porcelain` and report any file you
left uncommitted.

---
title: 'fix(visualMap): fix cursor is still pointer when `selectedMode` is disabled'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A dashboard author can configure a piecewise visualMap as read-only by setting `selectedMode: false`, for example when the legend-like scale is meant to explain colors without filtering data. Right now the control still advertises itself as clickable: hovering its pieces shows a pointer cursor even though clicking does nothing, which is misleading in polished analytical UIs.

  ## Desired outcome

  A piecewise visualMap with `selectedMode: false` should behave as a non-interactive display element, not as a disabled button that still looks active. Its symbols and labels should stop presenting click affordances while the normal selectable modes continue to behave exactly as they do today.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `selectedMode` is enabled, hovering the visualMap still shows the interactive cursor and selection behavior is unchanged. When `selectedMode: false`, the rendered pieces and their labels no longer expose a pointer cursor and should behave as silent display content rather than clickable controls.

  '
===
title: 'fix(visualMap): handle label collides with horizontal size visualMap'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A horizontal size visualMap can place its handle label in the same space as nearby UI, causing collisions that make the control hard to read or awkward to interact with. The overlap is a layout bug in a common dashboard configuration.


  ## Desired outcome

  Improve horizontal size-visualMap layout so the handle label avoids colliding with surrounding control elements and remains readable without manual spacing hacks from the chart author.


  ## Acceptance signals

  In the affected horizontal size visualMap layout, the handle label no longer overlaps the conflicting UI, the control stays legible and usable, and other visualMap layouts keep their current behavior.'

#!/bin/bash
# usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <file1> [file2...]
# Serialized (flock) per-requirement commit: stages ONLY the given paths.
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then echo "usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <paths...>" >&2; exit 2; fi
slug="$1"; shift
cd /workspace || exit 1
exec flock /tmp/echarts-git.lock /bin/bash -c '
  set -o pipefail
  slug="$1"; shift
  cd /workspace || exit 1
  if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
    echo "WARNING: index was not clean before staging; aborting to avoid cross-contamination" >&2
    git diff --cached --name-only >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  git add -- "$@" || exit 5
  git diff --cached --binary > "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" || exit 6
  if [ ! -s "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: empty patch for $slug (no changes in: $*)" >&2
    git reset -q
    exit 3
  fi
  git add -- "requirement_patches/$slug.diff"
  git commit -q -m "impl: $slug" || exit 7
  echo "COMMITTED $slug ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))"
' _ "$slug" "$@"

content.text: Both requirements are implemented, tested, typechecked, and committed. The remaining uncommitted files in the tree belong to other clusters (geo/MapDraw, pie scratch tests, agent_plans) — I did not touch them.

requirements.summary: Piecewise visualMap now reads `selectedMode` in doRender: the item symbol and its label get `silent = !selectMode` and `cursor = selectMode ? 'pointer' : 'default'`, and the itemGroup's `onclick` is only bound when selectedMode is truthy. _createItemSymbol gained a 4th `isSelectable` argument (upstream passes the raw selectMode value; equivalent). Selectable modes ('single'/'multiple'/true) are byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour since cursor 'pointer' and silent false are the zrender defaults.
requirements.notes: Verified against the real upstream diff (apache/echarts PR #20551, fetched via curl). Upstream relies on `silent` alone to suppress the pointer cursor (zrender skips hit-testing silent elements, so the cursor falls back to 'default'); I additionally set `cursor` explicitly because the requirement text and acceptance signals name the cursor. I also made the onclick binding conditional (requirement says "no click handler"); upstream left the binding in place, which is behaviourally identical because _onItemClick early-returns when !selectedMode. Skipped upstream's unused `PiecewiseVisualMapOption` import. New test: 3 cases (multiple / false / single) asserting cursor + silent + onclick on the rendered piece groups.

requirements.summary: In ContinuousView._updateHandle, hoisted `const align = this._applyTransform('left', shapes.mainGroup)` and, for `this._orient === 'horizontal'`, shift the handle label perpendicular to the bar by `minimumOffset = (align === 'left' || align === 'top') ? (itemSize[0] - symbolSize) / 2 : (itemSize[0] - symbolSize) / -2` before setStyle. The offset is 0 at the maximum symbolSize, so default (constant-symbolSize) horizontal layouts and all vertical layouts are untouched.
requirements.notes: This is an exact match of the upstream diff for apache/echarts PR #20249 (fetched via curl), minus upstream's unused `VerticalAlign` import which would trip lint. Root cause: when the visualMap maps `symbolSize`, the handle thumb is scaled down, which also scales the [handleSize, 0] handleLabelPoint offset, dragging the label back on top of the gradient bar at the low end. Measured in jsdom with itemWidth 20 / itemHeight 140 and inRange.symbolSize [0, 100]: min-end label y went from -24.67 (only 4.67px clear of the bar edge at -20) to -31.33 (11.33px clear); max-end label stays at -34. New test has 4 cases and I confirmed the key one fails when the new block is removed.
